description: Today and in the past, romantic love is a hotly contested theme in many kinds of narratives, including film, poetry, novels, plays, and cultural analyses. In this seminar, students write argumentative papers, interpretive essays, reflections, and other responses to love narratives from Shakespeare to early Hollywood film to contemporary memoir. The seminar will question why romantic love is such a widely celebrated subject, how it has changed over time, how its representation differs among cultures and subcultures, and how queer viewpoints, asexuality, and aromanticism have critiqued its assumptions. Class time will include discussion of assigned texts, workshopping of student writing, and in-class writing sessions.
